$comment: Accepted dependency advisories. CI (`scripts/audit-check.mjs`) fails on any
high/critical advisory NOT listed here, and fails on any listed exception
whose `expires` date has passed — so an exception can never quietly become
permanent. Every entry must state why the vulnerable code path is
An exception accepts the advisory ids it lists, and only those: a new advisory
on the same package fails the gate until it is reviewed and added by id.

exceptions.reason: Transitive via @nestjs/platform-express 11.2.3, which pins multer 2.2.0. All five are multipart/form-data parser defects: GHSA-wc9g-mqfw-jrwm (high, DoS via crafted field names, <2.3.0), GHSA-qfvm-cv95-jqjf (high, DoS via file-descriptor leak on aborted uploads, =2.2.0), GHSA-535w-7cp7-47q4 (high, DoS via oversized array index in field names, <2.3.0), GHSA-3pph-fpjx-jg34 (moderate, DoS via orphaned disk writes on aborted uploads, >=2.2.0 <2.4.0), GHSA-qvfw-j98x-7q72 (low, file-size limit bypass via async fileFilter race, <2.3.0). multer runs only when a route applies FileInterceptor/FilesInterceptor/AnyFilesInterceptor or registers MulterModule or multer middleware; apps/api does none of these (no multipart route in Phase 1C), and Express's own parsers handle JSON and urlencoded bodies only, so a multipart body is never parsed. A fix exists: @nestjs/platform-express >=11.2.6 pins multer 2.4.0, outside every listed range, within the declared ^11.2.3 — the expiry is short so the upgrade is decided rather than deferred. Supersedes the 2026 scaffold review of GHSA-4pg4-qvpc-4u3m, GHSA-g5hg-p3ph-g8qg, GHSA-44fp-w29j-9vj5 and GHSA-fjgf-rc76-4x9p, which no longer apply to the installed version.
